subject: Granular audit sampling vs full event streaming — decision inputs and owners
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Granular audit sampling vs full event streaming — decision inputs and owners

Hi team,

We need to make a call on how we expose audit/event retention and streaming options in the Console by EOW. Product wants two toggles: 
- "Full streaming": store all platform audit events for the selected retention window (30/90/365 days)
- "Tiered sampling": keep 100% of critical events + a sampled subset of lower-severity events (configurable sample rate)

Primary asks:
- Security: any compliance/regulatory blockers to offering sampling (SOC2, HIPAA posture) and what baseline guarantees we must keep?
- Infra: rough QPS/cost delta for sampling vs full for a mid-size customer (estimates attached).
- Dev/Product: UX constraints (do we need separate audit indices or a single schema?).

I've attached the current proposed audit_event_schema_v2.csv and a quick cost model (q3_cost_model_sampling_vs_full.xlsx). Can you each flag: mandatory non-negotiables, recommended defaults, and an owner to take this to implementation?

Also, Nimbus Health (cc later) asked whether SSO session IDs can be stitched to audit events when sampling is on — they need session linkage for investigations. If sampling drops 95% of low-severity events, how do we guarantee we still retain the minimal context?

Thanks — would like a triage note by Friday so I can update the roadmap doc.

Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: audit_event_schema_v2.csv (CSV), q3_cost_model_sampling_vs_full.xlsx (XLSX), sample-profiles.md (MD)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Granular audit sampling vs full event streaming — decision inputs and owners

Marissa — thanks for the clear ask. Quick notes from Security perspective: 

1) Compliance constraints
- SOC2: sampling is acceptable for lower-severity telemetry if you can demonstrate deterministic sampling logic and the ability to rehydrate (i.e., on-demand full capture for specific windows/queries). Audit trails used for attestation must be explainable; sampling must be documented and auditable.
- HIPAA/PHI contexts (e.g., Nimbus Health): we cannot sample away events that contain ePHI indicators. If we detect a patient identifier or PHI tag, that event must be preserved 100%.

2) Minimal guarantees we should expose as defaults
- Critical events (authn/authz failures, BYOK key ops, data export, admin console changes) -> always retained.
- Session linkage: always keep one event per session that contains the canonical session_id + last_activity timestamp. Sampling should never drop that anchor event.
- Sampling seed/version must be part of the metadata so auditors can reproduce which events were kept.

3) BYOK/KMS implications
- If customers use BYOK, audit events that show key usage/rotation must be captured fully for the retention window associated with key policies. Sampling that drops those could break forensic timelines.

4) Proposed defaults (for product):
- Default sampling rate: 10% for "info" level events, configurable down to 1% or up to 100% (full).
- Keep anchors per session and preserve all events flagged as PHI or critical.

5) Owners
- Security owner: karthik_iyer (I'll draft the compliance note).
- Infra owner to estimate cost: grace_oconnor.
- Product owner: marissa_cole.

I'm attaching a short checklist (referenced in the CSV) and will follow up with a short compliance note that you can include in the roadmap.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: SecOps Team <secops@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Granular audit sampling vs full event streaming — decision inputs and owners

On Thu, Sep 11, 2025 at 09:04, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa — thanks for the clear ask. Quick notes from Security perspective: 
> ...

Thanks — quick context from Nimbus: for incident investigations we require:
- Three months of full-fidelity logs for admin and data-export actions (we cannot accept sampling for these).
- Session stitching: our incident playbooks assume that at least 1 in 5 lower-severity events are retained, otherwise reconstruction becomes costly.
- We rely on SSO session_id linkage across events — if the "anchor" event is missing we lose a lot of context.

If you implement the session-anchor + deterministic sampling seed mentioned by Karthik, that should be fine. Also: any ability to request a temporary full-capture (on a per-account basis) for a forensics window would be a win for customers and reduce us having to pay for full-time full retention.

— Nimbus SecOps
secops@nimbushealth.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, SecOps Team <secops@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 23:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Granular audit sampling vs full event streaming — decision inputs and owners

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps (ACTIONABLE):

Summary decisions
- Keep-all for: critical events (auth failures, admin console changes, data exports, key ops).
- Session-anchor rule: keep one canonical event per session with session_id and last_activity — never sampled away.
- Default sampling: 10% for info-level events; configurable per-account. Deterministic seed/version metadata will be stored with each batch.
- BYOK: key usage/rotation events are in the always-keep list.
- For customers requiring higher fidelity (e.g., Nimbus): offer an "on-demand full-capture" window (30-day temporary full retention) as an add-on.

Owners / deliverables
- Karthik (security): write the compliance note and sample-documentation for SOC2/HIPAA impact (due 2025-09-22).
- Grace (infra): provide a bounded infra/cost implementation plan and deploy checklist (initial estimate due 2025-09-19).
- Marissa (product): update Console UX copy and add toggle + advanced config mocks (due 2025-09-24).
- Tessa (PM ops): consolidate requirements into INF-4221 and prepare the rollout playbook (due 2025-09-26).

Open questions
- How fast must historical "replay" be if a customer requests a temporary full-capture window? (Grace to propose SLOs).
- Do we need explicit contractual language for customers using BYOK about audit event retention? (Legal to advise; will loop on the next pass).

If no objections, I'll mark INF-4221 "ready for implementation" on Thursday.

Tessa Morgan
Program Manager, Product Operations
tessa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
